F D & C Colours Supplier

F D & C Colours Dyes are certified water-soluble synthetic food colorants. These can be manufactured as in powders, granules, and liquids form. The Anionic dyes have a sulphonic or carboxylic group. Cationic dyes have amino or aminomethyl as the basic group which is available as acid salts. Azo dyes have 1-3 azo bonds which makes the largest permitted food dye. These dyes absorb light and reflect a certain wavelength that is perceived as its color. Dyes need to be certified for their safety which is used as a food colorant or cosmetic colorant. A dye that is listed as “FD&C” is permitted by the Food & Drug Administration that can be added to foods, drugs, and cosmetics. “D&C” means the dye can be used only in drugs and cosmetics. Food Colourants can be dye, pigment, or substance that imparts colour when it is added to food or drink. It comes in many forms which consist of liquids, powders, gels, and pastes. It can be used in both commercial food production and domestic cooking. They can also be used in a variety of non-food applications which include cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, home craft projects, and medical devices. Food dyes products are valuable to us as they make the appearance of food and drinks more pleasant to taste. Drug dyes make the medicines more pleasing to the eye and can be easier to identify. Cosmetic dyes enhance beauty & allow more creativity.

Applications of F D & C Colours Dyes

F D & C Colours Dyes are used in a range of non-food applications including pharmaceuticals, home craft projects, cosmetics, and medical devices. They are also used both in domestic cooking and commercial food production.

Vat Dyes Supplier

Vat dyes are extensively and most significant dyes for cotton and cellulosic fibers dyeing and printing as they exhibit excellent fastness including perspiration, light, washing, chlorine, and rubbing fastness. Vat dyes are chemically complex dyes, insoluble in water, and need to be reduced to leuco form in sodium hydrosulphite alkaline solution before applying it to cotton/rayon fibers. Properties of Vat dyes:
  • Vat dyes are generally insoluble in water and natural colouring dyes.
  • The vatting process is necessary for making the insoluble vat dyes into a soluble form. The final colour is achieved by the oxidation process.
  • The dye is applied in a soluble and reduced form to permeate the fiber and then oxidized in the fiber back to its original insoluble form.
  • Any of a large class of water-insoluble dyes, such as indigo and the anthraquinone derivatives, are used particularly on cellulosic fibers.
  • Brilliant colours are attained in most shades as vat dyes are having especially washing fastness and lightfastness.

Applications of Vat Dyes

Vat dyes are extensively used for colouring cellulosic fiber especially cotton fiber. Vat dyes are widely used for running the dyeing process of cotton yarns used for producing jeans or denim products.

Powder Solvent Dyes Supplier

Powder Solvent dyes are soluble in organic solvents and are regularly used as a solution for organic solvents. Solvent dyes particularly come in red, blue, yellow, and green colours. Red and yellow solvent dyes are generally azo dyes, whereas the green and blue solvent dyes generally belong to anthraquinone dyes.

Properties of Powder Solvent Dyes

Powder Solvent Dyes are little polar or bipolar in nature and insoluble in water. They form a colloidal solution and do not undergo ionization. Powder Solvent Dyes are soluble in nonpolar solutions including in aromatic hydrocarbons, fats, alcohols, waxes, oils, etc. Powder Solvent dyes enhance colour with good consistency and have almost better lightfastness than other dyes and quality with their solid capacity of dissolving in organic solvents due to granular redisposition.

Applications of Powder Solvent Dyes

Powder Solvent dyes are extensively used for printing for marking inks, inkjet inks, gold imitation of metalized polyester films, and glass coloration. Used in the pyrotechnics industry for signalling smoke, and in the media industry for magazines and newspapers. Powder Solvent dyes are used to produce stains that identify with numerous cell structure components. PowderSolvent dyes are extensively used in the Plastic Industry, Medical Research / Diagnostics used for nylon, polyester, PMMA, PETP, colour acetates, acrylics, PVC, polystyrene, and styrene monomers. Solvent dyes are extensively used for Fibers, Filaments, Wood Stains, Metalized Polyester Films, Food Industry, Hydrocarbon Fuels, and Waxes.

Disperse Dyes Supplier

Disperse dyes are a class of non-ionic dyes, having low water solubility. Disperse dyes are generally available in powder form, prepared by milling the press cake with an approximate weight of an appropriate auxiliary chemicals and water, then drying, and mixing with suitable diluents which gives the dye product having 15–40% dye. As these particles have very fine particle size (≤1 μm) which provides a very large surface area aiding in dissolution which allows uptake by the fibre. The dyeing rate varies considerably according to the choice of dispersing agent used during the grinding process.

Properties of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are derivatives of azo, quinine anthraquinone, nitro groups. The chemical structure of most dyes are single azo class or mono azo class type, accounting for around 80% of all the dispersed dyes. Anthraquinone are about 15%, all other structures are about 5%. Disperse dyes are organic substances which are free of ionizing groups. Disperse dyes are non-soluble in water and in nature and a dispersing agent is needed for the dyeing process. As fastness properties especially light fastness and wet fastness are good to excellent they are widely used for dyeing synthetic fibers. Their dyeing process is carried out in high temperature and molecular size is smaller than other dyes.

Applications of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are mainly used for dyeing fabric of polyester yarn. Due to their chemical properties detailed above, disperse dyes are usually used for colouring synthetic fibers such as nylon, acrylic, polyester, and acetate rayon. Most types of polyester fabric lack ionic properties and are hydrophobic, which makes them very difficult to colour with other than disperse dyes. Disperse dyes are also used to dye resins and plastics for surface and general colouring uses.

Acid Dyes Supplier

Acid dyes are a water soluble class of dyes with anionic properties. These textile acid dyes are very effective for protein fibers such as wool, nylon, silk, and modified acrylics. Acid dyes are fixed to the fibers by hydrogen bonding, Vander Waals forces and ionic linkages. Properties of Acid dyes:
  • Since Acid dyes are sold as a sodium salt, therefore these form a large anion in the aqueous medium.
  • Acid dyes are anionic in nature.
  • Acid dyes are suitable for wool, silk, polyamide and modified acrylics.
  • Acid dyes are applied from a strongly acidic to neutral pH bath.
  • Acid dyes have no affinity for cotton cellulose, hence not suitable for cellulose.
  • Acid dyes combine with the fiber by hydrogen bonds, Vander Waals forces or through ionic linkages.

Applications of Acid Dyes

Acid dyes are mainly used to dye natural protein (wool and silk), synthetic polyamide (nylon), acrylics and blends of these fibres. Some acid dyes are used as food colorants, and some can also be used to stain organelles in the medical field.

Fast Colour Bases Supplier

Fast Colour Bases are extensively used in combination with Naphthols for Textile Dyeing & Printing. As Fast Colour Salts are stabilized with metal, they are easily soluble in water. There is no need of using Sodium Nitrate, Hydro-Chloride Acid. Fast Bases - Salts are highly sensitive to heat and moisture and need to be always stored in cool dry place. Being freely soluble in water, it is used in the dyeing process in two stages. The first stage involves material getting impregnated with naphthol solution. In the second stage, further development takes place with the use of a diazotized fast base. Combining chemically with naphthol, it gets absorbed by fiber thus providing insoluble dye on fiber. These can be used in different dyeing methods including tub-dip, open beck, jigger, circulating liquor and padding methods where different material to liquor ratio is used in different dyestuff concentrations for achieving defined shades. These dyes are skin friendly and easy to apply.

Applications of Fast Colour Bases

Fast Colour Bases find wide use in the textile industry in processes involving wax print and African print. Finding wide usage in textile, plastic, chemical and pharmaceutical industry, these when dyeing with naphthols offer economical usage. Vat dyes are extensively and most significant dyes for cotton and cellulosic fibers dyeing and printing as they exhibit excellent fastness including perspiration, light, washing, chlorine, and rubbing fastness. Vat dyes are chemically complex dyes, insoluble in water, and need to be reduced to leuco form in sodium hydrosulphite alkaline solution before applying it to cotton/rayon fibers. Properties of Vat dyes:
  • Vat dyes are generally insoluble in water and natural colouring dyes.
  • The vatting process is necessary for making the insoluble vat dyes into a soluble form. The final colour is achieved by the oxidation process.
  • The dye is applied in a soluble and reduced form to permeate the fiber and then oxidized in the fiber back to its original insoluble form.
  • Any of a large class of water-insoluble dyes, such as indigo and the anthraquinone derivatives, are used particularly on cellulosic fibers.
  • Brilliant colours are attained in most shades as vat dyes are having especially washing fastness and lightfastness.

Applications of Vat Dyes

Vat dyes are extensively used for colouring cellulosic fiber especially cotton fiber. Vat dyes are widely used for running the dyeing process of cotton yarns used for producing jeans or denim products.

Solvent dyes are soluble in organic solvents and are regularly used as a solution for organic solvents. Solvent dyes particularly come in red, blue, yellow, and green colours. Red and yellow solvent dyes are generally azo dyes, whereas the green and blue solvent dyes generally belong to anthraquinone dyes.

Solvent dyes are soluble in organic solvents and are regularly used as a solution for organic solvents. Solvent dyes particularly come in red, blue, yellow, and green colours. Disperse Dyes Supplier

Disperse dyes are a class of non-ionic dyes, having low water solubility. Disperse dyes are generally available in powder form, prepared by milling the press cake with an approximate weight of an appropriate auxiliary chemicals and water, then drying, and mixing with suitable diluents which gives the dye product having 15–40% dye. As these particles have very fine particle size (≤1 μm) which provides a very large surface area aiding in dissolution which allows uptake by the fibre. The dyeing rate varies considerably according to the choice of dispersing agent used during the grinding process.

Properties of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are derivatives of azo, quinine anthraquinone, nitro groups. The chemical structure of most dyes are single azo class or mono azo class type, accounting for around 80% of all the dispersed dyes. Anthraquinone are about 15%, all other structures are about 5%. Disperse dyes are organic substances which are free of ionizing groups. Disperse dyes are non-soluble in water and in nature and a dispersing agent is needed for the dyeing process. As fastness properties especially light fastness and wet fastness are good to excellent they are widely used for dyeing synthetic fibers. Their dyeing process is carried out in high temperature and molecular size is smaller than other dyes.

Applications of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are mainly used for dyeing fabric of polyester yarn. Due to their chemical properties detailed above, disperse dyes are usually used for colouring synthetic fibers such as nylon, acrylic, polyester, and acetate rayon. Most types of polyester fabric lack ionic properties and are hydrophobic, which makes them very difficult to colour with other than disperse dyes. Disperse dyes are also used to dye resins and plastics for surface and general colouring uses.

Disperse dyes are mainly used for dyeing fabric of polyester yarn. Disperse Dyes Supplier

Disperse dyes are a class of non-ionic dyes, having low water solubility. Disperse dyes are generally available in powder form, prepared by milling the press cake with an approximate weight of an appropriate auxiliary chemicals and water, then drying, and mixing with suitable diluents which gives the dye product having 15–40% dye. As these particles have very fine particle size (≤1 μm) which provides a very large surface area aiding in dissolution which allows uptake by the fibre. The dyeing rate varies considerably according to the choice of dispersing agent used during the grinding process.

Properties of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are derivatives of azo, quinine anthraquinone, nitro groups. The chemical structure of most dyes are single azo class or mono azo class type, accounting for around 80% of all the dispersed dyes. Anthraquinone are about 15%, all other structures are about 5%. Disperse dyes are organic substances which are free of ionizing groups. Disperse dyes are non-soluble in water and in nature and a dispersing agent is needed for the dyeing process. As fastness properties especially light fastness and wet fastness are good to excellent they are widely used for dyeing synthetic fibers. Their dyeing process is carried out in high temperature and molecular size is smaller than other dyes.

Applications of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are mainly used for dyeing fabric of polyester yarn. Due to their chemical properties detailed above, disperse dyes are usually used for colouring synthetic fibers such as nylon, acrylic, polyester, and acetate rayon. Most types of polyester fabric lack ionic properties and are hydrophobic, which makes them very difficult to colour with other than disperse dyes. Disperse dyes are also used to dye resins and plastics for surface and general colouring uses.

Acid Dyes Supplier

Acid dyes are a water soluble class of dyes with anionic properties. These textile acid dyes are very effective for protein fibers such as wool, nylon, silk, and modified acrylics. Acid dyes are fixed to the fibers by hydrogen bonding, Vander Waals forces and ionic linkages. Properties of Acid dyes:
  • Since Acid dyes are sold as a sodium salt, therefore these form a large anion in the aqueous medium.
  • Acid dyes are anionic in nature.
  • Acid dyes are suitable for wool, silk, polyamide and modified acrylics.
  • Acid dyes are applied from a strongly acidic to neutral pH bath.
  • Acid dyes have no affinity for cotton cellulose, hence not suitable for cellulose.
  • Acid dyes combine with the fiber by hydrogen bonds, Vander Waals forces or through ionic linkages.

Applications of Acid Dyes

Acid dyes are mainly used to dye natural protein (wool and silk), synthetic polyamide (nylon), acrylics and blends of these fibres. Some acid dyes are used as food colorants, and some can also be used to stain organelles in the medical field.

Reactive Dyes Supplier

Reactive Dyes chemically react with cellulose to form a covalent bond between the dye molecule and cellulose and with fiber polymer, becomes parts of the fiber. Reactive Dyes are organic dyes and are generally used for importing colour on cellulosic fibers. Properties of Reactive dyes:
  • Reactive dyes are anionic dyes that are soluble in water, found in liquid, powder, and print paste form.
  • Reactive dyes have good perspiration fastness, very good light fastness, and good wash fastness resulting in brighter shades.
  • Reactive dyes are economical, require low temperature, and less time for dyeing.

Applications of Reactive Dyes

Organic Pigments  have properties like superior heat stability, toxicity, tinting strength, staining and dispersion.   • All colors are lime-proof that allow these to be mixed with any suitable binding agent.

  • Shading pore filler pastes.
  • Wood Putties and Epoxy Paints.
  • Coloured waxes and Touch-up on furniture.

[elementor-template id="13303"] SD International is one of the leading supplier, and exporters of PU Foam Pigments. SD International offers PU Foam Pigments well known for using superior purity chemicals from trusted vendors to meet International Industry standards. S D International is one of the leading PU Foam Pigments exporters and suppliers of high grade and superior quality chemical products in Netherlands to an industry-wide customer base.

PU Foam Pigments Supplier

Polyurethane Colorants of very high quality are manufactured for specialized applications by using Pigments and other polymeric raw materials of only reputed makes with most appropriate specification. Intensive in-house development of specialized Colorants is done specially for Polyurethane Products with due consideration of hue, Chroma strength, opacity and of course at value for money price. Properties of PU Foam Pigments:
  • Excellent compatibility with the polyurethane system with proper binder ingredients.
  • High colour intensity pigment pastes with low loading to get desired colour characteristics.
  • Stable colorants to thermal degradation, chemical attack and radiation.
  • Consistency in colour shades and viscosity.
  • Non-fading and No fogging effects Specially designed color paste for automotive industry.
  • Compatible for both Polyester and Polyether Polyol based PU Systems.
  • High viscosity paste for blending in Polyol to get maximum yields.

Applications of PU Foam Pigments

  • PU Foam Pigments are used for Moulds & Tool Making.
  • PU Foam Pigments are used in Cushions, Foam Bedding, Automobile Industry.
  • PU Foam Pigments are used for Colouring Cast Moulded Components & Injection Moulding.
  • PU Foam Pigments are used for Coatings for pipeline, boats, shoe soles, sports equipment.
  • PU Foam Pigments are used for Sports Surfaces, Roofing & Flooring.

Fast Colour Bases Supplier

Fast Colour Bases are extensively used in combination with Naphthols for Textile Dyeing & Printing. As Fast Colour Salts are stabilized with metal, they are easily soluble in water. There is no need of using Sodium Nitrate, Hydro-Chloride Acid. Fast Bases – Salts are highly sensitive to heat and moisture and need to be always stored in cool dry place. Being freely soluble in water, it is used in the dyeing process in two stages. The first stage involves material getting impregnated with naphthol solution. In the second stage, further development takes place with the use of a diazotized fast base. Combining chemically with naphthol, it gets absorbed by fiber thus providing insoluble dye on fiber. These can be used in different dyeing methods including tub-dip, open beck, jigger, circulating liquor and padding methods where different material to liquor ratio is used in different dyestuff concentrations for achieving defined shades. These dyes are skin friendly and easy to apply.

Applications of Fast Colour Bases

Fast Colour Bases find wide use in the textile industry in processes involving wax print and African print. Finding wide usage in textile, plastic, chemical and pharmaceutical industry, these when dyeing with naphthols offer economical usage. Further, these are also used in achieving blue, maroon, yellow colour shades that are not possible with other dyestuff. These dyes possess superior colour fastness properties. These colour bases are widely used in:
  • Textile
  • Chemical
  • Pharmaceutical
  • Plastic

Acid Dyes Supplier

Acid dyes are a water soluble class of dyes with anionic properties. These textile acid dyes are very effective for protein fibers such as wool, nylon, silk, and modified acrylics. Acid dyes are fixed to the fibers by hydrogen bonding, Vander Waals forces and ionic linkages. Properties of Acid dyes:
  • Since Acid dyes are sold as a sodium salt, therefore these form a large anion in the aqueous medium.
  • Acid dyes are anionic in nature.
  • Acid dyes are suitable for wool, silk, polyamide and modified acrylics.
  • Acid dyes are applied from a strongly acidic to neutral pH bath.
  • Acid dyes have no affinity for cotton cellulose, hence not suitable for cellulose.
  • Acid dyes combine with the fiber by hydrogen bonds, Vander Waals forces or through ionic linkages.

Applications of Acid Dyes

Acid dyes are mainly used to dye natural protein (wool and silk), synthetic polyamide (nylon), acrylics and blends of these fibres. Some acid dyes are used as food colorants, and some can also be used to stain organelles in the medical field.

Acid Dyes Supplier

Acid dyes are a water soluble class of dyes with anionic properties. These textile acid dyes are very effective for protein fibers such as wool, nylon, silk, and modified acrylics. Acid dyes are fixed to the fibers by hydrogen bonding, Vander Waals forces and ionic linkages. Properties of Acid dyes:
  • Since Acid dyes are sold as a sodium salt, therefore these form a large anion in the aqueous medium.
  • Acid dyes are anionic in nature.
  • Acid dyes are suitable for wool, silk, polyamide and modified acrylics.
  • Acid dyes are applied from a strongly acidic to neutral pH bath.
  • Acid dyes have no affinity for cotton cellulose, hence not suitable for cellulose.
  • Acid dyes combine with the fiber by hydrogen bonds, Vander Waals forces or through ionic linkages.

Applications of Acid Dyes

Acid dyes are mainly used to dye natural protein (wool and silk), synthetic polyamide (nylon), acrylics and blends of these fibres. Some acid dyes are used as food colorants, and some can also be used to stain organelles in the medical field.

F D & C Colours Supplier

F D & C Colours Dyes are certified water-soluble synthetic food colorants. These can be manufactured as in powders, granules, and liquids form. The Anionic dyes have a sulphonic or carboxylic group. Cationic dyes have amino or aminomethyl as the basic group which is available as acid salts. Azo dyes have 1-3 azo bonds which makes the largest permitted food dye. These dyes absorb light and reflect a certain wavelength that is perceived as its color. Dyes need to be certified for their safety which is used as a food colorant or cosmetic colorant. A dye that is listed as “FD&C” is permitted by the Food & Drug Administration that can be added to foods, drugs, and cosmetics. “D&C” means the dye can be used only in drugs and cosmetics. Food Colourants can be dye, pigment, or substance that imparts colour when it is added to food or drink. It comes in many forms which consist of liquids, powders, gels, and pastes. It can be used in both commercial food production and domestic cooking. They can also be used in a variety of non-food applications which include cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, home craft projects, and medical devices. Food dyes products are valuable to us as they make the appearance of food and drinks more pleasant to taste. Drug dyes make the medicines more pleasing to the eye and can be easier to identify. Cosmetic dyes enhance beauty & allow more creativity.

Applications of F D & C Colours Dyes

F D & C Colours Dyes are used in a range of non-food applications including pharmaceuticals, home craft projects, cosmetics, and medical devices. They are also used both in domestic cooking and commercial food production.

[elementor-template id="13303"] SD International is one of the leading suppliers, and exporter of F D & C Colours. SD International offers F D & C Colours well known for using superior purity chemicals from trusted vendors to meet International Industry standards. S D International is one of the leading F D & C Colours exporters and suppliers of high grade and superior quality chemical products in Italy to an industry-wide customer base.

F D & C Colours Supplier

F D & C Colours Dyes are certified water-soluble synthetic food colorants. These can be manufactured as in powders, granules, and liquids form. The Anionic dyes have a sulphonic or carboxylic group. Cationic dyes have amino or aminomethyl as the basic group which is available as acid salts. Azo dyes have 1-3 azo bonds which makes the largest permitted food dye. These dyes absorb light and reflect a certain wavelength that is perceived as its color. Dyes need to be certified for their safety which is used as a food colorant or cosmetic colorant. A dye that is listed as “FD&C” is permitted by the Food & Drug Administration that can be added to foods, drugs, and cosmetics. “D&C” means the dye can be used only in drugs and cosmetics. Food Colourants can be dye, pigment, or substance that imparts colour when it is added to food or drink. It comes in many forms which consist of liquids, powders, gels, and pastes. It can be used in both commercial food production and domestic cooking. They can also be used in a variety of non-food applications which include cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, home craft projects, and medical devices. Food dyes products are valuable to us as they make the appearance of food and drinks more pleasant to taste. Drug dyes make the medicines more pleasing to the eye and can be easier to identify. Cosmetic dyes enhance beauty & allow more creativity.

Applications of F D & C Colours Dyes

F D & C Colours Dyes are used in a range of non-food applications including pharmaceuticals, home craft projects, cosmetics, and medical devices. They are also used both in domestic cooking and commercial food production.

Reactive Dyes Supplier

Reactive Dyes chemically react with cellulose to form a covalent bond between the dye molecule and cellulose and with fiber polymer, becomes parts of the fiber. Reactive Dyes are organic dyes and are generally used for importing colour on cellulosic fibers. Properties of Reactive dyes:
  • Reactive dyes are anionic dyes that are soluble in water, found in liquid, powder, and print paste form.
  • Reactive dyes have good perspiration fastness, very good light fastness, and good wash fastness resulting in brighter shades.
  • Reactive dyes are economical, require low temperature, and less time for dyeing.

Applications of Reactive Dyes

  • Reactive dyes are mainly used for cellulose fiber printing, polyamide fiber fabrics dyeing, and printing.
  • Reactive dyes are used for discharge printing, wool, polyester/stick blended fabric dyeing, and printing.
  • Reactive dyes are used in a knot, viscose, and their blended fabric dyeing and printing.

Vat Dyes Supplier

Vat dyes are extensively and most significant dyes for cotton and cellulosic fibers dyeing and printing as they exhibit excellent fastness including perspiration, light, washing, chlorine, and rubbing fastness. Vat dyes are chemically complex dyes, insoluble in water, and need to be reduced to leuco form in sodium hydrosulphite alkaline solution before applying it to cotton/rayon fibers. Properties of Vat dyes:
  • Vat dyes are generally insoluble in water and natural colouring dyes.
  • The vatting process is necessary for making the insoluble vat dyes into a soluble form. The final colour is achieved by the oxidation process.
  • The dye is applied in a soluble and reduced form to permeate the fiber and then oxidized in the fiber back to its original insoluble form.
  • Any of a large class of water-insoluble dyes, such as indigo and the anthraquinone derivatives, are used particularly on cellulosic fibers.
  • Brilliant colours are attained in most shades as vat dyes are having especially washing fastness and lightfastness.

Applications of Vat Dyes

Vat dyes are extensively used for colouring cellulosic fiber especially cotton fiber. Vat dyes are widely used for running the dyeing process of cotton yarns used for producing jeans or denim products.

name: Solvent Dyes Manufacturer in India
description:

Solvent Dyes Supplier

Solvent dyes are soluble in organic solvents and are regularly used as a solution for organic solvents. Solvent dyes particularly come in red, blue, yellow, and green colours. Red and yellow solvent dyes are generally azo dyes, whereas the green and blue solvent dyes generally belong to anthraquinone dyes.

Properties of Solvent Dyes

Solvent Dyes are little polar or bipolar in nature and insoluble in water. They form a colloidal solution and do not undergo ionization. Solvent Dyes are soluble in nonpolar solutions including in aromatic hydrocarbons, fats, alcohols, waxes, oils, etc. Solvent dyes enhance colour with good consistency and have almost better lightfastness than other dyes and quality with their solid capacity of dissolving in organic solvents due to granular redisposition.

Applications of Solvent Dyes

Solvent dyes are extensively used for printing for marking inks, inkjet inks, gold imitation of metalized polyester films, and glass coloration. Used in the pyrotechnics industry for signalling smoke, and in the media industry for magazines and newspapers. Solvent dyes are used to produce stains that identify with numerous cell structure components. Solvent dyes are extensively used in the Plastic Industry, Medical Research / Diagnostics used for nylon, polyester, PMMA, PETP, colour acetates, acrylics, PVC, polystyrene, and styrene monomers. Solvent dyes are extensively used for Fibers, Filaments, Wood Stains, Metalized Polyester Films, Food Industry, Hydrocarbon Fuels, and Waxes.

name: Disperse Dyes Manufacturer in India
description:
[elementor-template id="13303"]
SD International is one of the leading suppliers, and exporter of Disperse dyes. S D International is one of the leading Disperse dyes exporters and suppliers of high grade and superior quality chemical products in India to an industry-wide customer base.

Disperse Dyes Supplier

Disperse dyes are a class of non-ionic dyes, having low water solubility. Disperse dyes are generally available in powder form, prepared by milling the press cake with an approximate weight of an appropriate auxiliary chemicals and water, then drying, and mixing with suitable diluents which gives the dye product having 15–40% dye. As these particles have very fine particle size (≤1 μm) which provides a very large surface area aiding in dissolution which allows uptake by the fibre. The dyeing rate varies considerably according to the choice of dispersing agent used during the grinding process.

Properties of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are derivatives of azo, quinine anthraquinone, nitro groups. The chemical structure of most dyes are single azo class or mono azo class type, accounting for around 80% of all the dispersed dyes. Anthraquinone are about 15%, all other structures are about 5%. Disperse dyes are organic substances which are free of ionizing groups. Disperse dyes are non-soluble in water and in nature and a dispersing agent is needed for the dyeing process. As fastness properties especially light fastness and wet fastness are good to excellent they are widely used for dyeing synthetic fibers. Their dyeing process is carried out in high temperature and molecular size is smaller than other dyes.

Applications of Disperse Dyes

Disperse dyes are mainly used for dyeing fabric of polyester yarn. Due to their chemical properties detailed above, disperse dyes are usually used for colouring synthetic fibers such as nylon, acrylic, polyester, and acetate rayon. Most types of polyester fabric lack ionic properties and are hydrophobic, which makes them very difficult to colour with other than disperse dyes. Disperse dyes are also used to dye resins and plastics for surface and general colouring uses.

Acid Dyes Supplier

Acid dyes are a water soluble class of dyes with anionic properties. These textile acid dyes are very effective for protein fibers such as wool, nylon, silk, and modified acrylics. Acid dyes are fixed to the fibers by hydrogen bonding, Vander Waals forces and ionic linkages. Properties of Acid dyes:
  • Since Acid dyes are sold as a sodium salt, therefore these form a large anion in the aqueous medium.
  • Acid dyes are anionic in nature.
  • Acid dyes are suitable for wool, silk, polyamide and modified acrylics.
  • Acid dyes are applied from a strongly acidic to neutral pH bath.
  • Acid dyes have no affinity for cotton cellulose, hence not suitable for cellulose.
  • Acid dyes combine with the fiber by hydrogen bonds, Vander Waals forces or through ionic linkages.

Applications of Acid Dyes

Acid dyes are mainly used to dye natural protein (wool and silk), synthetic polyamide (nylon), acrylics and blends of these fibres. Some acid dyes are used as food colorants, and some can also be used to stain organelles in the medical field.
